threads.body: `SpanExpectation` now supports mapping-only expectations (no `expect` block / `count=None`), so the docstring statement that “Every span in the report must be selected by some expectation” is no longer generally true. Please update the docstring to reflect the new semantics (exactness only when assertions are present).

`input.sample.span.kind` can be reported as `client`, `CLIENT`, or `SPAN_KIND_CLIENT` depending on exporter. Using the raw kind in the span-type suffix match can prevent `_expected_for_op` from finding the registry span type, silently skipping expected-attribute checks for valid spans.

This issue also appears on line 184 of the same file.

threads.body:
`.id` is the member's semconv identifier, not the value instrumentation puts on the span, and the new rego compares this set against the value read off a real span. It lines up today only because `gen_ai.operation.name` defines `id == value`; this same template resolves the HTTP model, where `http.request.method` is `id: connect` / `value: "CONNECT"`.

```suggestion
             value: [.type.members[]?.value]
```
The comment just above still tells the reader to keep `_known_operation_names` in sync with `model/gen-ai/registry.yaml` by hand — that is the maintenance this rule removes. Drop the sentence.
